⭐ 5C HAS MEMORY -- IT IS NOT A VOLTAGE LOOKUP. Unplugged after somewhat more than 15 min on the charger (read at 14:03, so ~20 min) following the 24 h run. Debug page 5C reads 96-97 (96 a minute earlier) at a pack of 4.00 V. Yesterday 09:52 the pack was 3.99 V and 5C read ~85. Same voltage, 12 points apart: no curve does that. 5C therefore carries state anchored to the last charge, not a reading of the pack.

Also kills surface-charge relaxation as the explanation: had the pack been inflated by charging it would read 4.05-4.10 and sag. It read 4.00, one hundredth above where the run ended, so ~15 min added almost nothing. The pack is honest; the gauge is not.

NEXT (cheap, decisive): stay on battery with the lighting fixed and watch 5C for 2-4 h. The pack drifts only ~0.008 V/h, so it is effectively a CONSTANT input -- any 5C movement is the module's own dynamics. If it walks 97 -> ~85 it is a slow filter of pack voltage with an hours-long time constant (usable, ignore for hours after a charge). If it stalls at 94-96 until the pack moves, its anchor is the last charge and it is closer to a time-since-charge counter than a gauge. ⚠️ Keep the RGB effect fixed: a varying load moves terminal voltage and makes meter pairs incomparable.

⭐⭐ VDD IS NOT AN LDO OUTPUT AND HAS NO DROPOUT AHEAD OF IT. Debug page: 5C 78%, VDD 3.901 V. Meter at the pack: 3.84 V. ⚠️ VDD IS HIGHER THAN THE PACK -- impossible for a linear regulator, so it is a buck-boost. Over the whole excursion so far the pack has fallen 4.18 -> 3.84 V (-340 mV) while VDD moved 3.90 -> 3.901 (+1 mV).

⚠️ This falsifies 'VDD will follow the pack, a dropout below it, once the pack gets down to around 3.95-4.0 V' in docs/battery.md. The pack is now well past that and VDD has not moved. VDD is useless as a pack gauge across the entire practical range, and the planned two-region gauge (5C above the dropout, ADC below) has no lower region to hand over to. 5C is the ONLY signal.

⚠️ SAFETY: the warn (3.55 V) and RGB cut (3.40 V) thresholds are set on VDD, which is pinned at 3.90. The firmware's low-battery net may be inert, with the pack's own protection doing the real work. Worth confirming before any deep run.
